title: Research construction: rescale JP8 coefficient work across magnitudes (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The selected #626 JP8 cleanup prepares each dyadic coefficient independently. This finite circuit contribution reuses its private work stream across consecutive **different coefficient magnitudes** related by powers of two, preserving source values and target-update order. It saves **10,338 additional real-component primitives beyond the equal-magnitude sharing in #722**.

**Status: research construction / finite complex-supplier circuit improvement; no new κ.**

| Complete scalar program | Original | Equal-magnitude sharing (#722 method) | Rescaling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JP8 forward | 257,232 | 237,544 | **227,206** |
| JP8 inverse-transpose | 257,280 | 257,280 | 257,280 |

The 30,026 total saving includes #722's 19,688; only the additional 10,338 is new here. All source reads, Horner preparation, doubling/halving, signed accumulation and clearing are charged. The original exact prefix envelopes and paid recursive profiles are unchanged. This is an operation count, not a runtime benchmark.

Only `research/complex-coefficient-rescaling/` is added. It contains executable primitive circuits, all 1,015 block certificates, a written substitution/cost argument, five source pins, an independent DP and scalar-basis checker, negative controls and a local sprint claim. No pending implementation is imported.

The local interface requires clearing private work at **block boundaries**, replacing the selected emitter's per-macro clearing contract inside those blocks. Production-emitter integration and refreshed invoices remain future work. No additional helper, frame transition or recursive child is introduced. The selected supplier, `upstream/`, global ownership and frontier pointer are unchanged. Inherited compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape/recovery, bit-supplier and analytic assumptions remain; this is not a formal multiplication theorem.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-coefficient-rescaling/verify.py
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_JP8_COEFFICIENT_RESCALING incremental_real_saved=10338 blocks=1015 columns=716 orientations=2 controls=11
```

- Both fixed 27,909-event programs are checked. The complete scalar projections cover all 716 live input columns and arbitrary incoming coefficient work. All 591 distinct JP8 add/scale cases are checked; changed blocks execute literal primitives.
- A separate implementation evaluates 18,925 forward candidate blocks and confirms the restricted optimum. All 6,279 touched-register/work basis cases pass. The 1,211 new magnitude-changing edges are distinguished from 2,023 equal-magnitude edges.
- The full negative census retains 49 nonprofitable transitions (28 ties, 21 losses) and 1,015 incompatible odd-numerator transitions. Backward has no eligible join in this class. No broader circuit-optimality claim.
- Eleven primary controls, four independent semantic controls, and nine additional tests pass, including all 343 signed triples over a seven-value domain, source/receipt corruption, early-ended helpers, relocation and gzip recompression.
- CPython 3.14.7 and 3.11.14 on macOS arm64 pass, including isolated optimized execution. Ruff, local documentation links, staged whitespace and `make selected-record-check` pass.
- Full `make verify`, selected cold replay, global admission, Linux CI and Lean were not run for this isolated research addition.

## Provenance and coordination

Exact base: **`66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`**. Selected #626 source: `660de893d27bb7abd1d5b01b1640207528a5c851`; #622 construction: `f69477f4f6d3c7eb1f740b166881bffed4ffa9f6`; retained #543: `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`. Full gzip payloads and exact plain-file bytes are pinned; native/event hashes additionally match the preserved #626 SPEC.

OS assignment seed **39**, complex-supplier track, selected JP8 by parity. Three candidates and the claim are recorded locally because no pinned coordination issue exists. The final overlap refresh covered **556 open PRs through #737**. #722 is the direct methodological predecessor and comparison. #696/#723 and concurrent #734 optimize individual coefficient preparations; this uses ordinary Horner preparation and shares work between macros. No combined saving with those lowerings is asserted. #681, #698 and #719 cover distinct factory, frame and CK rank questions.

Credit to @ellipsi2's #722, Jeremy Kothe/AtomScout and the #622 lineage, Chafik Boukhalfa's #626 package, icekylinx's scalar/emitter work, DreamingOfClouds, Dugongue, eumemic (including #411), Sagar Thakrar, Chris Pagolu and all retained predecessor notices. Prepared for **Jeffrey Cox (@namredips)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, including one scoped AI reviewer who supplied the independent checker. Apache-2.0; no independent human-review claim.
